pull.title: KAFKA-21230: Pause processing on uncommitted bytes
pull.body:
During a long rebalance, a `StreamThread` can use native memory without
limit and fail with an out-of-memory error. When the uncommitted state
store bytes exceed `statestore.uncommitted.max.bytes`,
`StreamThread#maybeCommit` forces a commit. But `TaskManager` skips
commits during a rebalance, and `runOnceWithoutProcessingThreads`
continues to process records. Thus the uncommitted bytes continue to
increase. RocksDB keeps these bytes in a `WriteBatch` in native memory,
outside the block cache and the write buffers.

At the start of each iteration of the processing loop, `StreamThread`
now calls `maybePauseProcessingForUncommittedBytes()`, which checks
`shouldCommitDueToUncommittedBytes()`. Because `maybeCommit` commits at
the end of each iteration, the bytes exceed the limit at this point only
when that commit was skipped or failed. So the check needs no extra
state. While processing is paused, the thread does not process records
or run punctuators, because both write to the state stores. It continues
to poll, so the rebalance can complete, and it continues to call
`maybeCommit`. Processing resumes when a commit succeeds, or when a
commit on partition revocation flushes the buffers. The thread logs the
pause and the resume at INFO level.

This change decreases throughput during a long rebalance, but it
prevents the out-of-memory error. `GlobalStreamThread` does not need
this change, because one thread writes to its stores, checks the bytes
and flushes them, and nothing skips that flush. A separate pull request
will apply the same pause to processing threads.

Two new `StreamThreadTest` tests cover the change.
`shouldNotProcessOrPunctuateWhileUncommittedBytesExceedLimit` shows that
the thread polls and tries to commit, but does not process or punctuate,
while the commit is skipped.
`shouldResumeProcessingOnceUncommittedBytesAreCommitted` shows that
processing stays paused for the iteration in which the rebalance
completes, and resumes only after the commit succeeds.

review_comments.body: With exactly-once processing, transactional stores, and caching disabled, `Processor.init()` can buffer more than the byte limit before `StreamTask.commitNeeded()` becomes true. This guard then blocks the processing and punctuation that would make the task commit-eligible, while `TaskExecutor` skips its `prepareCommit()` and `postCommit()`, leaving the entire thread paused indefinitely even without a rebalance. Make buffered initialization writes commit-eligible before applying this guard, and add a regression test covering initialization writes above the limit.
@nicktelford can you take a look at this - seems to be a valid condition

With a per-thread limit below the aggregate empty-batch overhead (for example, a one-byte limit with a transactional RocksDB store), this guard pauses processing and punctuation indefinitely, even without a rebalance. `RocksDBTransactionBuffer.approximateNumUncommittedBytes()` includes the fixed header of an empty `WriteBatch`, and successful commits recreate that nonzero baseline rather than clearing the condition. Exclude empty-batch overhead from the shared byte accounting and add a real-store regression test with a limit below that baseline.

The fix is to change `RocksDBTransactionBuffer.approximateNumUncommittedBytes()` to only count the `WriteBatch` size once it starts containing records.

This also fixes a false-positive introduced in our previous change: we would request a commit unconditionally after the topology was initialized, because `RocksDBTransactionBuffer.approximateNumUncommittedBytes()` would never be `0`. Now it can be, so we now only request an initialization commit if at least one record was written by the initialization process.

commit.message:
KAFKA-21230: Pause processing while uncommitted bytes exceed limit

During a long rebalance, a StreamThread can use native memory without
bound and fail with an out-of-memory error. When the uncommitted state
store bytes exceed statestore.uncommitted.max.bytes,
StreamThread#maybeCommit forces a commit. But TaskManager skips commits
during a rebalance, and runOnceWithoutProcessingThreads continues to
process records. Thus the uncommitted bytes, which RocksDB keeps in a
WriteBatchWithIndex in native memory, continue to increase.

At the start of each iteration of the processing loop, StreamThread now
calls maybePauseProcessingForUncommittedBytes(), which checks
shouldCommitDueToUncommittedBytes(). Because maybeCommit commits at the
end of each iteration, the bytes exceed the limit at this point only
when that commit was skipped or failed. While processing is paused, the
thread does not process records or run punctuators, because both write
to the state stores. It continues to poll and to call maybeCommit.
Processing resumes when a commit succeeds, or when a commit on partition
revocation flushes the buffers. The pause and the resume are logged at
INFO level.

Processor.init() can also write to transactional stores. Such a task
has no records processed, so it is not eligible for commit, and the
pause can hold it with nothing to process. When initialization of the
topology leaves uncommitted bytes in the stores, StreamTask now marks
the task as needing a commit, so that the next commit drains them.

This change decreases throughput during a long rebalance, but prevents
the out-of-memory error. A separate change will apply the same limit to
processing threads.

commit.message:
KAFKA-21230: Exclude empty WriteBatch overhead from uncommitted bytes

RocksDBTransactionBuffer.approximateNumUncommittedBytes() included the
fixed header of an empty WriteBatch, which no commit releases. With a
per-thread limit below the total of these headers, processing stayed
paused after every commit. The empty header also made StreamTask
request a commit after every restoration of a task with a transactional
RocksDB store.

The buffer now counts the WriteBatch only when it holds writes. The
integration test is renamed to UncommittedBytesLimitIntegrationTest and
gets a test with a one-byte limit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

issue.title: KAFKA-21230: Pause task executors on byte limit

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
#23728 pauses processing and punctuation while the uncommitted state
store bytes of a StreamThread exceed `statestore.uncommitted.max.bytes`.
That pause is in `runOnceWithoutProcessingThreads`. When processing
threads are enabled, task executors process records and run punctuators
independently of the StreamThread loop, so the pause does not stop them.
If a commit is skipped during a rebalance, or fails, the executors
continue to write to the state stores. The uncommitted bytes then
increase without bound, and the native memory of the transaction buffers
increases with them.

`StreamThread#maybePauseProcessingForUncommittedBytes()` now also sets
the pause on the processing threads, through the new
`TaskManager#setProcessingThreadsPaused`. `runOnceWithProcessingThreads`
calls it after `maybeCommit`. The scheduling `TaskManager` gains
`setProcessingPaused` and `processingPaused`.

`DefaultTaskManager` keeps the flag in a volatile field for each
StreamThread. It does not use `TaskExecutionMetadata`, because all
StreamThreads share that object. While the flag is set, `canProgress`
returns false, so `assignNextTask` assigns no task and
`awaitProcessableTasks` blocks. When processing resumes,
`DefaultTaskManager` signals the executors. While paused,
`DefaultTaskExecutor` does not process or punctuate its current task.
The task makes no progress, so the executor releases it through the
existing path for such tasks.

`GlobalStreamThread` does not need this change. One thread writes,
checks and flushes synchronously, and no condition skips the flush.

Both tests in `UncommittedBytesLimitIntegrationTest` now also run with
processing threads enabled.
